205: if(APPLE OR LINUX OR WIN32)
206:     # Three reasons for setting CMAKE_RUNTIME_OUTPUT_DIRECTORY.
207:     # - Normalize the output directory so it is the same regardless of
208:     #   single or multi-config generator. Note that wrapping this in a
209:     #   generator expression forces multi-configuration generators (like
210:     #   Visual Studio, Xcode or Ninja multi-config) to take the exact path
211:     #   and not add  a further $<CONFIG> to it;
212:     # - Build all executables into a common output directory.
213:     # - On Windows, build dlls into the same directory as the executables,
214:     #   so they can find their dlls when run in the build directory.
215:     set(CMAKE_RUNTIME_OUTPUT_DIRECTORY $<1:${KTX_BUILD_DIR}/$<CONFIG>>)
216: 
217:     # Reason for setting CMAKE_LIBRARY_OUTPUT_DIRECTORY.
218:     # - On GNU/Linux and macOS build .{so,dylib}s into the same directory
219:     #   as the executables so that the INSTALL RPATH we need to add to
220:     #   installed binaries is functional in the build directory as well.
221:     set(CMAKE_LIBRARY_OUTPUT_DIRECTORY $<1:${KTX_BUILD_DIR}/$<CONFIG>>)
222: 
223:     # For GNU/Linux and macOS BUILD_WITH_INSTALL_RPATH is necessary to have
224:     # the install rpath set duing build. See below for more explanation.
225:     set(CMAKE_BUILD_WITH_INSTALL_RPATH ON)
226: 
227:     # Notes about install names, rpaths and code signing
228:     # --------------------------------------------------
229:     # Changing the install name of a library by setting INSTALL_NAME_DIR
230:     # on a library target will invalidate the signature as it causes
231:     # cmake to run `install_name_tool` after building and signing. The
232:     # default install name is the library target's name prefixed by `@rpath/`.
233:     # With this, `dyld` will load the library provided it is in one of the
234:     # directories specified by a program's INSTALL_RPATH or is in the
235:     # directory part of a full-path name passed to `dlopen`. Because it would
236:     # also invalidate the signature INSTALL_RPATH cannot be altered
237:     # during install. Hence BUILD_WITH_INSTALL_RPATH.
238:     #
239:     # On macOS, a bad signature in either executable or shared library is
240:     # indicated by the executable exiting with "Killed: 9".
241:     #
242:     # Although GNU/Linux code is not currently being signed, handle its
243:     # INSTALL_RPATH the same way for symmetry.

59: option( LIBKTX_FEATURE_ETC_UNPACK "ETC decoding support." ON )

206: macro(common_libktx_settings target enable_write library_type)

208:     if(TARGET mkvk)

236:         PUBLIC

241:                 BASE_DIRS include ../external/dfdutils/

595: ####################################################
596: # ASTC Encoder.
597: ####################################################
598: 
599: # Determine most of the ASTC-related settings automatically.
600: 
601: # On Linux and Windows only one architecture is supported at once. On
602: # macOS simultaneous multiple architectures are supported by the ASTC
603: # encoder but not by the BasisU encoder. The latter supports only SSE
604: # SIMD that is enabled by compile time defines which makes it not amenable
605: # to a standard Xcode universal binary build. To ensure BASISU_SSE
606: # is disabled when building for multiple architectures use only the
607: # value of CMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES to decide if a universal build
608: # has been requested. Do not expose the astc-encoder's
609: # ASTCENC_UNIVERSAL_BUILD configuration option.
610: 
611: set(universal_build OFF)
612: if("${CMAKE_SYSTEM_NAME}" STREQUAL "Darwin")
613:     # Check CMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES for multiple architectures.
614:     list(FIND CMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES "$(ARCHS_STANDARD)" archs_standard)
615:     list(LENGTH CMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES architecture_count)
616:     if(NOT ${archs_standard} EQUAL -1 OR architecture_count GREATER 1)
617:         set(universal_build ON)
618:     endif()
619:     # Set ordinary variable to override astc-encoder option's ON default
620:     # and hide the option.
621:     set(ASTCENC_UNIVERSAL_BUILD ${universal_build})
622: endif()
623: 
624: # If we detect the user is doing a universal build defer to astc-encoder
625: # to pick the architectures. If a universal build has not been requested,
626: # present options to the user to turn off SIMD and, if running on x86_64
627: # to choose which SIMD ISA to use. On arm64 always use Neon. On unknown
628: # CPUs use None.
629: #
630: # On x86_64, if neither ASTCENC_ISA_SSE41 nor ASTCENC_ISA_SSE2 are defined,
631: # choose ASTCENC_ISA_AVX2. If ASTCENC_ISA_AVX2 fails to compile user must
632: # choose another x86_64 option.
633: 
634: if(NOT ${universal_build})
635:     set(ASTCENC_ISA_NATIVE OFF)
636:     set(ASTCENC_ISA_NEON OFF)
637:     if(NOT CPU_ARCHITECTURE STREQUAL x86_64)
638:         set(ASTCENC_ISA_AVX2 OFF)
639:         set(ASTCENC_ISA_SSE41 OFF)
640:         set(ASTCENC_ISA_SSE2 OFF)
641:     endif()
642: 
643:     # "" in the CACHE sets causes use of the existing documentation string.
644:     if(${ASTCENC_ISA_NONE})
645:         set(ASTCENC_LIB_TARGET astcenc-none-static)
646:         if(CPU_ARCHITECTURE STREQUAL x86_64)
647:             set(ASTCENC_ISA_AVX2 OFF CACHE BOOL "" FORCE)
648:             set(ASTCENC_ISA_SSE41 OFF CACHE BOOL "" FORCE)
649:             set(ASTCENC_ISA_SSE2 OFF CACHE BOOL "" FORCE)
650:         endif()
651:     else()
652:         if(CPU_ARCHITECTURE STREQUAL x86_64)
653:             if (${ASTCENC_ISA_SSE41})
654:                 set(ASTCENC_LIB_TARGET astcenc-sse4.1-static)
655:                 set(ASTCENC_ISA_AVX2 OFF CACHE BOOL "" FORCE)
656:                 set(ASTCENC_ISA_SSE2 OFF CACHE BOOL "" FORCE)
657:             elseif (${ASTCENC_ISA_SSE2})
658:                 set(ASTCENC_LIB_TARGET astcenc-sse2-static)
659:                 set(ASTCENC_ISA_AVX2 OFF CACHE BOOL "" FORCE)
660:                 set(ASTCENC_ISA_SSE41 OFF CACHE BOOL "" FORCE)
661:             else()
662:                 set(ASTCENC_LIB_TARGET astcenc-avx2-static)
663:                 set(ASTCENC_ISA_AVX2 ON CACHE BOOL "" FORCE)
664:                 set(ASTCENC_ISA_SSE41 OFF CACHE BOOL "" FORCE)
665:                 set(ASTCENC_ISA_SSE2 OFF CACHE BOOL "" FORCE)
666:             endif()
667:         elseif(CPU_ARCHITECTURE STREQUAL armv8 OR CPU_ARCHITECTURE STREQUAL arm64)
668:             set(ASTCENC_LIB_TARGET astcenc-neon-static)
669:             set(ASTCENC_ISA_NEON ON)
670:             set(ASTCENC_ISA_NONE OFF CACHE BOOL "" FORCE)
671:         else()
672:             message(STATUS "Unsupported ISA for ASTC on ${CPU_ARCHITECTURE} arch, using ASTCENC_ISA_NONE.")
673:             set(ASTCENC_ISA_NONE ON CACHE BOOL "" FORCE)
674:             set(ASTCENC_LIB_TARGET astcenc-none-static)
675:         endif()
676:     endif()
677: endif()

# Macro for common lib settings

macro(common_libktx_settings target enable_write library_type)

    if(TARGET mkvk)
        # Creating vulkan headers only required after Vulkan Spec/SDK updates.
        add_dependencies(${target} mkvk)
    endif()

    set_target_properties(${target} PROPERTIES
        VERSION ${PROJECT_VERSION}
        SOVERSION ${PROJECT_VERSION_MAJOR}
        XCODE_ATTRIBUTE_ENABLE_HARDENED_RUNTIME "YES"
    )

    if(APPLE_LOCKED_OS)
        set_target_properties(${target} PROPERTIES
            FRAMEWORK TRUE
        )
        set_source_files_properties(
            include/ktx.h
            PROPERTIES MACOSX_PACKAGE_LOCATION Headers
        )
        set_source_files_properties(
            ${KTX_ROOT_DIR}/external/dfdutils/KHR/khr_df.h
            PROPERTIES MACOSX_PACKAGE_LOCATION Headers/KHR
        )
    else()
        # Use a FILE_SET instead of PUBLIC_HEADER because with the latter
        # the KHR subdirectory cannot be preserved.
        # Sadly FILE_SETs may not be added to FRAMEWORK targets.
        target_sources(${target}
        PUBLIC
            FILE_SET public_headers
                # FILE_SET supports having the KHR subdirectory. However a FILE SET
                # cannot be used with frameworks so keep using PUBLIC_HEADER for that
                TYPE HEADERS
                BASE_DIRS include ../external/dfdutils/
                FILES
                    include/ktx.h
                    ../external/dfdutils/KHR/khr_df.h
        )
    endif()

    if( NOT ${library_type} STREQUAL STATIC )
        # Must not call this macro for static libs on Windows. To keep
        # the if test simple, never call it for static libs. On macOS
        # and iOS Xcode knows libs aren't signed so it would ignore the
        # settings made by this macro.
        set_code_sign(${target} "NOPPS")
    endif()

    if(MSVC)
        target_compile_options( ${target} PRIVATE /W4;$<$<BOOL:${LIBKTX_WERROR}>:/WX> )
        target_compile_options( ${target} PRIVATE $<IF:$<CONFIG:Debug>,/Gz,/O2> )
        # Enable UTF-8 support
        target_compile_options( ${target} PRIVATE $<$<C_COMPILER_ID:MSVC>:/utf-8> )
        target_compile_options( ${target} PRIVATE $<$<CXX_COMPILER_ID:MSVC>:/utf-8> )
    elseif(${CMAKE_CXX_COMPILER_ID} STREQUAL "GNU"
           OR ${CMAKE_CXX_COMPILER_ID} MATCHES "Clang")
        target_compile_options( ${target} PRIVATE -Wall -Wextra $<$<BOOL:${LIBKTX_WERROR}>:-Werror>)
        target_compile_options( ${target} PRIVATE $<IF:$<CONFIG:Debug>,-O0$<SEMICOLON>-g,-O3> )
        if(EMSCRIPTEN)
            target_link_options( ${target} PRIVATE $<IF:$<CONFIG:Debug>,-gsource-map,-O3> )
        else()
            target_link_options( ${target} PRIVATE $<IF:$<CONFIG:Debug>,-g,-O3> )
        endif()
        if(APPLE)
            target_compile_options(${target} PRIVATE $<$<BOOL:${LIBKTX_EMBED_BITCODE}>:-fembed-bitcode>)
        endif()
    else()
        message(FATAL_ERROR "${CMAKE_CXX_COMPILER_ID} not yet supported.")
    endif()

    # To influence the FP settings of apps depending on us do this. Unsure if that is
    # a wise thing hence commented.
    #target_compile_options( ${target} PUBLIC ${fp_options} )

    target_compile_definitions(
        ${target}
    PUBLIC
        "$<$<CONFIG:Debug>:_DEBUG;DEBUG>"
    PRIVATE
        LIBKTX
        SUPPORT_SOFTWARE_ETC_UNPACK=$<IF:$<BOOL:${LIBKTX_FEATURE_ETC_UNPACK}>,1,0>
    )

    # C/C++ Standard
    # Need c11 for Unicode string literals. Need c++17 because some basisu
    # include files have c++17 features.
    target_compile_features(${target} PUBLIC c_std_11 cxx_std_17)

    # Compiler Warning Flags
    if(EMSCRIPTEN)
        target_compile_options(${target} PRIVATE
            -Wno-nested-anon-types
            -Wno-gnu-anonymous-struct
        )
    else()
        target_compile_options(${target} PRIVATE
            # clang options
            $<$<CXX_COMPILER_ID:AppleClang,Clang>:
                -Wno-nested-anon-types
                -Wno-gnu-anonymous-struct
            >
            $<$<CXX_COMPILER_ID:GNU>:
                -Wno-cast-function-type
            >
            # not clang options
            $<$<NOT:$<CXX_COMPILER_ID:MSVC>>:
                -Wno-pedantic
            >
        )
    endif()

    target_include_directories(
        ${target}
    PUBLIC
        # N.B. PUBLIC HEADER FILE_SET adds its BASE_DIRS to INTERFACE_INCLUDE_DIRECTORIES.
        # Unfortunately FILE_SET cannot be used when building a framework (iOS) so keep
        # this. It does result in `include` being in the list twice. Tolerate the duplicate
        # entry over YAI (yet another if).
        $<BUILD_INTERFACE:${CMAKE_CURRENT_LIST_DIR}/include>
        $<INSTALL_INTERFACE:include>
    PRIVATE
        $<BUILD_INTERFACE:${KTX_ROOT_DIR}/external>
        $<BUILD_INTERFACE:${KTX_ROOT_DIR}/utils>
        ${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/external/dfdutils
    )

    target_include_directories(
        ${target}
    SYSTEM PRIVATE
        ${KTX_ROOT_DIR}/other_include
    )

    if( ${library_type} STREQUAL STATIC )
        target_compile_definitions(${target} PUBLIC KHRONOS_STATIC)
    endif()

    # To reduce size, don't support transcoding to ancient formats.
    target_compile_definitions(${target} PRIVATE BASISD_SUPPORT_FXT1=0)

    if(WIN32)
        target_compile_definitions(
            ${target}
        PRIVATE
            # Only set dllexport when building a shared library.
            $<$<STREQUAL:${library_type},SHARED>:KTX_API=__declspec\(dllexport\)>
            # Code compiled with the versions shown defaults to a constexpr
            # std::mutex constructor and requires a mscvp140.dll of at least
            # version 14.40.33810.00 otherwise code creating a mutex
            # crashes mysteriously. Since many JVM installations bundle
            # their own version of the VC++ redistributables chances are
            # high they will not have a modern enough version so JNI modules
            # linked with libktx will crash when multiple threads are used,
            # as they are in the BasisU and ASTC encoders.
            #
            # To avoid this set a define to prevent the compiler using
            # constexpr mutex constructors. Remove this eventually after
            # in-use JVM installations have at least this VC runtime. Remove
            # also from ASTCENC_LIB_TARGET settings around line 1169.
            $<$<AND:${is_msvccl},$<VERSION_GREATER_EQUAL:$<CXX_COMPILER_VERSION>,19.40.33811>>:_DISABLE_CONSTEXPR_MUTEX_CONSTRUCTOR>
            $<$<AND:${is_clangcl},$<VERSION_GREATER_EQUAL:$<CXX_COMPILER_VERSION>,17.0.3>>:_DISABLE_CONSTEXPR_MUTEX_CONSTRUCTOR>
        PUBLIC # only for basisu_c_binding.
            BASISU_NO_ITERATOR_DEBUG_LEVEL
        )
        # The generator automatically sets the needed VCLinker
        # option when a .def file is seen in sources.
        # C++ names are mangled differently according to compiler and ABI.
        # Only internalexport_write has a c++ name.
        if(MINGW)
            target_sources(
                ${target}
            PRIVATE
                def/internalexport.def
                $<${enable_write}:def/internalexport_write_mingw.def>
            )
            # Need these flags if mingw happens to target the ucrt (new) rather
            # than the legacy msvcrt. Otherwise tests will fail to run because
            # the necessary dlls will be missing. If we statically link
            # them instead it's fine. This does not cause any abberations if
            # the mingw toolchain targets msvcrt instead.
            target_link_options(${target} PUBLIC -static-libgcc -static-libstdc++)
        else()
            target_sources(
                ${target}
            PRIVATE
                def/internalexport.def
                $<${enable_write}:def/internalexport_write.def>
            )
        endif()
    elseif(EMSCRIPTEN)
        target_compile_definitions(${target} PRIVATE
            # To reduce size, don't support transcoding to formats not
            # supported # by WebGL.
            BASISD_SUPPORT_ATC=0
            BASISD_SUPPORT_PVRTC2=0
            # Don't support higher quality mode to avoid 64k table.
            BASISD_SUPPORT_ASTC_HIGHER_OPAQUE_QUALITY=0
            KTX_OMIT_VULKAN=1
        )
        target_link_options(${target} INTERFACE
#            "SHELL:-s ASSERTIONS=2"
#            "SHELL:-s SAFE_HEAP=1"
#            "SHELL:-s STACK_OVERFLOW_CHECK=2"
            "SHELL:-s ALLOW_MEMORY_GROWTH=1"
            "SHELL:-s MALLOC=emmalloc"
            "SHELL:-s FULL_ES3=1"
            "SHELL:-s GL_ENABLE_GET_PROC_ADDRESS=1" # For Emscripten 3.1.51+
        )
    endif()

    if(LIBKTX_FEATURE_KTX1)
        target_compile_definitions(${target} PUBLIC KTX_FEATURE_KTX1)
        target_sources(
            ${target}
        PRIVATE
            src/texture1.c
            src/texture1.h
        )
    endif()

    if(LIBKTX_FEATURE_KTX2)
        target_compile_definitions(${target} PUBLIC KTX_FEATURE_KTX2)
    endif()

    if(MINGW AND TARGET Threads::Threads AND CMAKE_USE_PTHREADS_INIT)
        target_compile_definitions(${target} PRIVATE WIN32_HAS_PTHREADS)
    endif()

    if(LIBKTX_FEATURE_VK_UPLOAD)
        target_sources(
            ${target}
        PRIVATE
            include/ktxvulkan.h
            src/vk_funcs.c
            src/vk_funcs.h
            src/vkloader.c
        )
        if(APPLE_LOCKED_OS)
            set_source_files_properties(
                include/ktxvulkan.h
                PROPERTIES MACOSX_PACKAGE_LOCATION Headers
            )
        else()
            target_sources(
                ${target}
            PUBLIC
                FILE_SET public_headers
                FILES
                    include/ktxvulkan.h
            )
        endif()

        target_include_directories(
            ${target}
        PRIVATE
            $<BUILD_INTERFACE:${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/../external/dfdutils>
            $<INSTALL_INTERFACE:../external/dfdutils>
        )
    else()
        target_compile_definitions( ${target} PRIVATE KTX_OMIT_VULKAN=1 )
    endif()

    # Adding write capability to target ktx
    if(${enable_write})
        target_compile_definitions(
            ${target}
        PUBLIC
            KTX_FEATURE_WRITE
        PRIVATE
            BASISU_SUPPORT_OPENCL=$<IF:$<BOOL:${BASISU_OPENCL}>,1,0>
        )
        target_compile_options(
            ${target}
        PRIVATE
            $<$<AND:$<BOOL:${BASISU_SSE}>,$<CXX_COMPILER_ID:AppleClang,Clang,GNU>>:
                -msse4.1
            >
        )
        if(EMSCRIPTEN)
            target_link_options(
                ${target}
            INTERFACE
                # Default 64kb not enough for encode_uastc.
                "SHELL:-s STACK_SIZE=96kb"
            )
        endif()
        target_link_libraries(
            ${target}
        PRIVATE
            $<$<BOOL:${BASISU_OPENCL}>:${OpenCL_LIBRARY}>
        )
    endif()

endmacro(common_libktx_settings)

macro(add_lib_dependencies target lib)

        target_sources(${target} PRIVATE $<TARGET_OBJECTS:${lib}>)

    else()
        target_link_libraries(${target} PRIVATE ${lib})
    endif()
endmacro(add_lib_dependencies)

####################################################
# ASTC Encoder.
####################################################

# Determine most of the ASTC-related settings automatically.

# On Linux and Windows only one architecture is supported at once. On
# macOS simultaneous multiple architectures are supported by the ASTC
# encoder but not by the BasisU encoder. The latter supports only SSE
# SIMD that is enabled by compile time defines which makes it not amenable
# to a standard Xcode universal binary build. To ensure BASISU_SSE
# is disabled when building for multiple architectures use only the
# value of CMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES to decide if a universal build
# has been requested. Do not expose the astc-encoder's
# ASTCENC_UNIVERSAL_BUILD configuration option.

set(universal_build OFF)
if("${CMAKE_SYSTEM_NAME}" STREQUAL "Darwin")
    # Check CMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES for multiple architectures.
    list(FIND CMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES "$(ARCHS_STANDARD)" archs_standard)
    list(LENGTH CMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES architecture_count)
    if(NOT ${archs_standard} EQUAL -1 OR architecture_count GREATER 1)
        set(universal_build ON)
    endif()
    # Set ordinary variable to override astc-encoder option's ON default
    # and hide the option.
    set(ASTCENC_UNIVERSAL_BUILD ${universal_build})
endif()

# If we detect the user is doing a universal build defer to astc-encoder
# to pick the architectures. If a universal build has not been requested,
# present options to the user to turn off SIMD and, if running on x86_64
# to choose which SIMD ISA to use. On arm64 always use Neon. On unknown
# CPUs use None.
#
# On x86_64, if neither ASTCENC_ISA_SSE41 nor ASTCENC_ISA_SSE2 are defined,
# choose ASTCENC_ISA_AVX2. If ASTCENC_ISA_AVX2 fails to compile user must
# choose another x86_64 option.

if(NOT ${universal_build})
    set(ASTCENC_ISA_NATIVE OFF)
    set(ASTCENC_ISA_NEON OFF)
    if(NOT CPU_ARCHITECTURE STREQUAL x86_64)
        set(ASTCENC_ISA_AVX2 OFF)
        set(ASTCENC_ISA_SSE41 OFF)
        set(ASTCENC_ISA_SSE2 OFF)
    endif()

    # "" in the CACHE sets causes use of the existing documentation string.
    if(${ASTCENC_ISA_NONE})
        set(ASTCENC_LIB_TARGET astcenc-none-static)
        if(CPU_ARCHITECTURE STREQUAL x86_64)
            set(ASTCENC_ISA_AVX2 OFF CACHE BOOL "" FORCE)
            set(ASTCENC_ISA_SSE41 OFF CACHE BOOL "" FORCE)
            set(ASTCENC_ISA_SSE2 OFF CACHE BOOL "" FORCE)
        endif()
    else()
        if(CPU_ARCHITECTURE STREQUAL x86_64)
            if (${ASTCENC_ISA_SSE41})
                set(ASTCENC_LIB_TARGET astcenc-sse4.1-static)
                set(ASTCENC_ISA_AVX2 OFF CACHE BOOL "" FORCE)
                set(ASTCENC_ISA_SSE2 OFF CACHE BOOL "" FORCE)
            elseif (${ASTCENC_ISA_SSE2})
                set(ASTCENC_LIB_TARGET astcenc-sse2-static)
                set(ASTCENC_ISA_AVX2 OFF CACHE BOOL "" FORCE)
                set(ASTCENC_ISA_SSE41 OFF CACHE BOOL "" FORCE)
            else()
                set(ASTCENC_LIB_TARGET astcenc-avx2-static)
                set(ASTCENC_ISA_AVX2 ON CACHE BOOL "" FORCE)
                set(ASTCENC_ISA_SSE41 OFF CACHE BOOL "" FORCE)
                set(ASTCENC_ISA_SSE2 OFF CACHE BOOL "" FORCE)
            endif()
        elseif(CPU_ARCHITECTURE STREQUAL armv8 OR CPU_ARCHITECTURE STREQUAL arm64)
            set(ASTCENC_LIB_TARGET astcenc-neon-static)
            set(ASTCENC_ISA_NEON ON)
            set(ASTCENC_ISA_NONE OFF CACHE BOOL "" FORCE)
        else()
            message(STATUS "Unsupported ISA for ASTC on ${CPU_ARCHITECTURE} arch, using ASTCENC_ISA_NONE.")
            set(ASTCENC_ISA_NONE ON CACHE BOOL "" FORCE)
            set(ASTCENC_LIB_TARGET astcenc-none-static)
        endif()
    endif()
endif()

# setting ASTCENC_DECOMPRESSOR to ON breaks the build, so force it to OFF
# and hide it from cmake-gui (by using type INTERNAL)
set(ASTCENC_DECOMPRESSOR OFF CACHE INTERNAL "")
set(ASTCENC_CLI OFF) # Only build as library not the CLI astcencoder
# Force static build for astc-encoder
set(BUILD_SHARED_LIBS OFF)
add_subdirectory(../external/astc-encoder astc-encoder)
set(BUILD_SHARED_LIBS ${BUILD_SHARED_LIBS_RESET})
set_property(TARGET ${ASTCENC_LIB_TARGET} PROPERTY POSITION_INDEPENDENT_CODE ON)

target_compile_definitions(
    ${ASTCENC_LIB_TARGET}
PRIVATE
    # ASTC encoder uses std::mutex. For more info. see comment about same

Building KTX

KTX uses the the [CMake](https://cmake.org) build system. Depending on your
platform and how you configure it, it will create project/build files (e.g. an Xcode project, a Visual Studio solution or Make files) that allow you to
build the software and more (See [CMake generators](https://cmake.org/cmake/help/latest/manual/cmake-generators.7.html)).

KTX consist of the following parts

- The `libktx` main library
- Command line tools (for Linux / macOS / Windows)
- Load test applications (for [OpenGL<sup>®</sup> 3](https://www.khronos.org/opengl), [OpenGLES<sup>®</sup>](https://www.khronos.org/opengles) or [Vulkan<sup>®</sup>](https://www.khronos.org/vulkan))

The minimal way to a build is to clone this repository and follow the instructions for your desired build below.

_libktx_ only
-------------
To build only _libktx_ and nothing else, run the following in a terminal

# This generates build/project files in the clone's `lib/build` subfolder
cmake . -B build

# Compile the project
cmake --build build

## Version 5.0.0-rc1

### Summary

This is a major release. Although the reason for bumping the major number is a small but incompatible change in the *libktx* API, there are major changes throughout the software:

* __`ktxBasisParams` API has two incompatible changes.__
* Support for the Binomial UASTC HDR formats has been added to all supported API bindings and relevant tools.
* The *ktx* tool suite is now a superset of the legacy tools.
* __The legacy tools have been removed.__
* A CMake project has been added to build *libktx*.
* Source code of dependencies is no longer included in CMake target source lists. All dependencies are now built by their own CMake projects and linked to *libktx*.

This is a pre-release because the version of the KTX specification with which it is compliant, Document Revision 5, has not yet been published. The source of the draft is available at https://github.com/KhronosGroup/KTX-Specification/pull/216.

### New Features in v5.0
#### Tools

* Images can be encoded to the Binomial *UASTC HDR 4x4* and *UASTC HDR 6x6 Intermediate* formats in __*ktx create*__ and __*ktx encode*__. Images in these formats can be transcoded to ASTC HDR or BC6H Unsigned formats.
* __*ktx extract*__ can extract images in ASTC HDR formats from KTX v2 files. It writes them to  `.exr` files. It will apply `KTXmapRange` during extraction.
* __*ktx create*__ accepts a `--premultiply-alpha` option.
* __*ktx create*__ can resize or scale its input files, except `.raw`.
* __*ktx create*__ accepts file name listing files as input. Prefix the name of such a file with `@` or `@@`.
* __*ktx convert*__ for converting KTX v1 files.

This shows the equivalent new tool for each removed legacy tool.

| Legacy Tool | `ktx` tool |
| :---------: | :--------: |
| ktx2ktx2 | convert -t ktx |
| ktx2check | validate |
| ktxinfo | info |
| ktxsc | deflate or encode |
| toktx | create |

 
#### *libktx* functions

* `ktxTexture2_CompressBasisEx` can  now encode to Binomial *UASTC HDR 4x4* and *UASTC HDR 6x6 Intermediate* formats. There are two incompatible changes in the struct `ktxBasisParams` passed to this function:
    * `ktx_bool_t uastc` is now `ktx_basis_codec_e codec` which accepts the following values
        * `KTX_BASIS_CODEC_NONE`
        * `KTX_BASIS_CODEC_ETC1S`
        * `KTX_BASIS_CODEC_UASTC_LDR_4x4`
        * `KTX_BASIS_CODEC_UASTC_HDR_4x4`
        * `KTX_BASIS_CODEC_UASTC_HDR_6x6_INTERMEDIATE`
    * `compressionLevel` is now named `etc1sCompressionLevel`
* `ktxTexture2_DecodeAstc` can now decode ASTC HDR files.
* `ktxTexture2_TranscodeBasis` can transcode images in *UASTC HDR 4x4* and *UASTC HDR 6x6 Intermediate* formats to ASTC HDR or BC6H Unsigned.
  
The new functionality is exposed in the Java, JavaScript and Python bindings.

### Notable Fixes in v5.0

* A crash in ___ktx create___ when reading tiled `.exr` files has been fixed.
* An extra swizzle, when generating mip levels when the output image components are not in RGBA order, leading to incorrect colors in some mip levels has been

149: /**

152:  * @brief Construct a ktxVulkanDeviceInfo object.

154:  * Records the device information, allocates a command buffer that will be
155:  * used to transfer image data to the Vulkan device and retrieves the physical
156:  * device memory properties for ease of use when allocating device memory for
157:  * the images.
158:  *
159:  * If @c VK_IMAGE_TILING_OPTIMAL will be passed to ktxTexture\_VkUploadEx(), the
160:  * family of the @a queue parameter must support transfers. This is true if
161:  * any of @c VK_QUEUE_GRAPHICS_BIT, @c VK_QUEUE_COMPUTE_BIT or
162:  * @c VK_QUEUE_TRANSFER_BIT is set in the @c queueFlags property of the queue's
163:  * @c VkQueueFamilyProperties. If protected memory is being used, i.e
164:  * @c queueFlags has the @c VK_QUEUE_PROTECTED_BIT set, then
165:  * @c VK_IMAGE_TILING_OPTIMAL must be passed to ktxTexture\_VkUploadEx().
166:  *
167:  * VkImages created in @ref ktxTexture::ktxTexture\_VkUploadEx()
168:  * "ktxTexture_VkUploadEx()" will have @c VK_SHARING_MODE_EXCLUSIVE set.
169:  * Thus the resulting image will be usable only with queues of the same family
170:  * as @a queue.
171:  *
172:  * Pass a valid ktxVulkanDeviceInfo\* to any Vulkan KTX image loading
173:  * function to provide it with the information.
174:  *
175:  * @returns KTX\_SUCCESS on success, other  KTX\_\* enum values on error.
176:  *
177:  * @exception KTX_NOT_FOUND   A dynamically loaded Vulkan function
178:  *                            required by the loader was not found.
179:  *
180:  * @exception KTX_OUT_OF_MEMORY A command buffer could not be allocated.
181:  *
182:  * @sa ktxVulkanDeviceInfo\_Destruct()
183:  *
184:  * @param  This            pointer to the ktxVulkanDeviceInfo object to
185:  *                        initialize.
186:  * @param  physicalDevice handle of the Vulkan physical device.
187:  * @param  device         handle of the Vulkan logical device.
188:  * @param  queue          handle of the Vulkan queue.
189:  * @param  cmdPool        handle of the Vulkan command pool.
190:  * @param  pAllocator     pointer to the allocator to use for the image
191:  *                        memory. If NULL, the default allocator will be used.
192:  *
193:  */
194: KTX_error_code
195: ktxVulkanDeviceInfo_Construct(ktxVulkanDeviceInfo* This,
196:                               VkPhysicalDevice physicalDevice, VkDevice device,
197:                               VkQueue queue, VkCommandPool cmdPool,
198:                               const VkAllocationCallbacks* pAllocator)
199: {
200:    return ktxVulkanDeviceInfo_ConstructEx(This, VK_NULL_HANDLE, physicalDevice, device, queue,
201:                                           cmdPool, pAllocator, NULL);
202: }

204: /**
205:  * @memberof ktxVulkanDeviceInfo
206:  * @copydoc ktxVulkanDeviceInfo_Construct
207:  *
208:  * @~English
209:  * @param  instance       handle of the Vulkan instance. If @c VK_NULL_HANDLE,
210:  *                        which is not recommended, the function will attempt
211:  *                        to initialize the instance-level functions via the
212:  *                        platform's standard dynamic library symbol loading
213:  *                        mechanisms.
214:  * @param  pFunctions     pointer to the struct of functions to use for vulkan
215:  *                        operations. Can be NULL in which case the function
216:  *                        will retrieve the proc addresses itself.
217:  */
218: KTX_error_code
219: ktxVulkanDeviceInfo_ConstructEx(ktxVulkanDeviceInfo* This,
220:                               VkInstance instance,
221:                               VkPhysicalDevice physicalDevice, VkDevice device,
222:                               VkQueue queue, VkCommandPool cmdPool,
223:                               const VkAllocationCallbacks* pAllocator,
224:                               const ktxVulkanFunctions* pFunctions)
225: {
226: 
227: #define LOAD_EXT_FUNC(member, fun) \
228: do {                             \
229:   if ((member).fun == NULL) {            \
230:     (member).fun = (PFN_##fun)ktxLoadVulkanFunction(#fun); \
231:     if ((member).fun == NULL) {          \
232:         return KTX_NOT_FOUND;                         \
233:     }\
234:   } \
235: } while (0)
236: 
237: #define LOAD_INST_FUNC(member, instance, fun) \
238: do {                             \
239:   if ((member).fun == NULL) {            \
240:     (member).fun = (PFN_##fun)((member).vkGetInstanceProcAddr)((instance), #fun); \
241:     if ((member).fun == NULL) {          \
242:         return KTX_NOT_FOUND;                         \
243:     }\
244:   } \
245: } while (0)
246: 
247: #define LOAD_DEVICE_FUNC(member, device, fun) \
248: do {                             \
249:   if ((member).fun == NULL) {            \
250:     (member).fun = (PFN_##fun)((member).vkGetDeviceProcAddr)((device), #fun); \
251:     if ((member).fun == NULL) {          \
252:         return KTX_NOT_FOUND;                         \
253:     }\
254:   } \
255: } while (0)
256: 
257: 
258:     This->instance = instance;
259:     This->physicalDevice = physicalDevice;
260:     This->device = device;
261:     This->queue = queue;
262:     This->cmdPool = cmdPool;
263:     This->pAllocator = pAllocator;
264: 
265:     ktxVulkanFunctions funcs;
266:     memset(&funcs, 0, sizeof(ktxVulkanFunctions));
267: 
268:     if (pFunctions != NULL)
269:         funcs = *pFunctions;
270: 
271:     if (instance == VK_NULL_HANDLE || pFunctions == NULL) {
272:         // This is the old behavior, where no functions where specified. We
273:         // take a shot at loading them dynamically.
274: 
275:         // The reason we check this here, is that ktxLoadVulkanFunction doesn't
276:         // give us a proper error code.
277:         ktx_error_code_e kresult = ktxLoadVulkanLibrary();
278:         if (kresult != KTX_SUCCESS)
279:             return kresult;
280: 
281:         // If pFunctions are null, then we try to load the minimum number of
282:         // required functions.
283:         if (pFunctions == NULL) {
284:             LOAD_EXT_FUNC(funcs, vkGetInstanceProcAddr);
285:         }
286: 
287:         // If we have no instance, we will need to bind the instance-level
288:         // functions, as we won't be able to load them through
289:         // vkGetInstanceProcAddr, and we need to load vkGetDeviceProcAddr.
290:         if (instance == VK_NULL_HANDLE) {
291:             LOAD_EXT_FUNC(funcs, vkGetDeviceProcAddr);
292: 
293:             // These require an instance, which we don't have.
294:             LOAD_EXT_FUNC(funcs, vkGetPhysicalDeviceFormatProperties);
295:             LOAD_EXT_FUNC(funcs, vkGetPhysicalDeviceImageFormatProperties);
296:             LOAD_EXT_FUNC(funcs, vkGetPhysicalDeviceMemoryProperties);
297:         }
298:     }
299: 
300:     // We now load the rest of the functions in.
301:     LOAD_INST_FUNC(funcs, instance, vkGetPhysicalDeviceFormatProperties);
302:     LOAD_INST_FUNC(funcs, instance, vkGetPhysicalDeviceMemoryProperties);
303:     LOAD_INST_FUNC(funcs, instance, vkGetPhysicalDeviceImageFormatProperties);
304: 
305: 
306:     // We now get to device functions.
307:     LOAD_INST_FUNC(funcs, instance, vkGetDeviceProcAddr);
308: 
309:     LOAD_DEVICE_FUNC(funcs, device, vkAllocateCommandBuffers);
310:     LOAD_DEVICE_FUNC(funcs, device, vkFreeCommandBuffers);
311:     LOAD_DEVICE_FUNC(funcs, device, vkAllocateMemory);
312:     LOAD_DEVICE_FUNC(funcs, device, vkFreeMemory);
313:     LOAD_DEVICE_FUNC(funcs, device, vkBeginCommandBuffer);
314:     LOAD_DEVICE_FUNC(funcs, device, vkEndCommandBuffer);
315:     LOAD_DEVICE_FUNC(funcs, device, vkBindBufferMemory);
316:     LOAD_DEVICE_FUNC(funcs, device, vkBindImageMemory);
317:     LOAD_DEVICE_FUNC(funcs, device, vkCmdBlitImage);
318:     LOAD_DEVICE_FUNC(funcs, device, vkCmdCopyBufferToImage);
319:     LOAD_DEVICE_FUNC(funcs, device, vkCmdPipelineBarrier);
320:     LOAD_DEVICE_FUNC(funcs, device, vkCreateImage);
321:     LOAD_DEVICE_FUNC(funcs, device, vkDestroyImage);
322:     LOAD_DEVICE_FUNC(funcs, device, vkCreateBuffer);
323:     LOAD_DEVICE_FUNC(funcs, device, vkDestroyBuffer);
324:     LOAD_DEVICE_FUNC(funcs, device, vkCreateFence);
325:     LOAD_DEVICE_FUNC(funcs, device, vkDestroyFence);
326:     LOAD_DEVICE_FUNC(funcs, device, vkWaitForFences);
327:     LOAD_DEVICE_FUNC(funcs, device, vkMapMemory);
328:     LOAD_DEVICE_FUNC(funcs, device, vkUnmapMemory);
329:     LOAD_DEVICE_FUNC(funcs, device, vkQueueSubmit);
330:     LOAD_DEVICE_FUNC(funcs, device, vkQueueWaitIdle);
331:     LOAD_DEVICE_FUNC(funcs, device, vkGetBufferMemoryRequirements);
332:     LOAD_DEVICE_FUNC(funcs, device, vkGetImageMemoryRequirements);
333:     LOAD_DEVICE_FUNC(funcs, device, vkGetImageSubresourceLayout);
334: 
335: 
336:     This->vkFuncs = funcs;
337: 
338:     VkCommandBufferAllocateInfo cmdBufInfo = {
339:             .sType = VK_STRUCTURE_TYPE_COMMAND_BUFFER_ALLOCATE_INFO
340:     };
341:     VkResult result;
342: 
343:     This->vkFuncs.vkGetPhysicalDeviceMemoryProperties(physicalDevice,
344:                                         &This->deviceMemoryProperties);
345: 
346:     // Use a separate command buffer for texture loading. Needed for
347:     // submitting image barriers and converting tilings.
348:     cmdBufInfo.commandPool = cmdPool;
349:     cmdBufInfo.level = VK_COMMAND_BUFFER_LEVEL_PRIMARY;
350:     cmdBufInfo.commandBufferCount = 1;
351:     result = This->vkFuncs.vkAllocateCommandBuffers(device, &cmdBufInfo,
352:                                                     &This->cmdBuffer);
353:     if (result != VK_SUCCESS) {
354:         return KTX_OUT_OF_MEMORY; // TODO: Consider an equivalent to pGlError
355:     }
356:     return KTX_SUCCESS;
357: 
358: #undef LOAD_EXT_FUNC
359: #undef LOAD_INST_FUNC
360: #undef LOAD_DEVICE_FUNC
361: }

421: typedef struct user_cbdata_optimal {
422:     VkBufferImageCopy* region; // Specify destination region in final image.
423:     VkDeviceSize offset;       // Offset of current level in staging buffer
424:     ktx_uint32_t numFaces;
425:     ktx_uint32_t numLayers;
426:     // The following are used only by optimalTilingPadCallback
427:     ktx_uint8_t* dest;         // Pointer to mapped staging buffer.
428:     ktx_uint32_t elementSize;
429:     ktx_uint32_t numDimensions;
430: #if defined(_DEBUG)
431:     VkBufferImageCopy* regionsArrayEnd;
432: #endif
433: } user_cbdata_optimal;
434: 
435: /**
436:  * @internal
437:  * @~English
438:  * @brief Callback for optimally tiled textures with no source row padding.
439:  *
440:  * Images must be preloaded into the staging buffer. Each iteration, i.e.
441:  * the value of @p faceLodSize must be for a complete mip level, regardless of
442:  * texture type. This should be used only with @c ktx_Texture_IterateLevels.
443:  *
444:  * Sets up a region to copy the data from the staging buffer to the final
445:  * image.
446:  *
447:  * @note @p pixels is not used.
448:  *
449:  * @copydetails PFNKTXITERCB
450:  */
451: static KTX_error_code
452: optimalTilingCallback(int miplevel, int face,
453:                       int width, int height, int depth,
454:                       ktx_uint64_t faceLodSize,
455:                       void* pixels, void* userdata)
456: {
457:     user_cbdata_optimal* ud = (user_cbdata_optimal*)userdata;
458:     UNUSED(pixels);
459: 
460:     // Set up copy to destination region in final image
461: #if defined(_DEBUG)
462:     assert(ud->region < ud->regionsArrayEnd);
463: #endif
464:     ud->region->bufferOffset = ud->offset;
465:     ud->offset += faceLodSize;
466:     // These 2 are expressed in texels.
467:     ud->region->bufferRowLength = 0;
468:     ud->region->bufferImageHeight = 0;
469:     ud->region->imageSubresource.aspectMask = VK_IMAGE_ASPECT_COLOR_BIT;
470:     ud->region->imageSubresource.mipLevel = miplevel;
471:     ud->region->imageSubresource.baseArrayLayer = face;
472:     ud->region->imageSubresource.layerCount = ud->numLayers * ud->numFaces;
473:     ud->region->imageOffset.x = 0;
474:     ud->region->imageOffset.y = 0;
475:     ud->region->imageOffset.z = 0;
476:     ud->region->imageExtent.width = width;
477:     ud->region->imageExtent.height = height;
478:     ud->region->imageExtent.depth = depth;
479: 
480:     ud->region += 1;
481: 
482:     return KTX_SUCCESS;
483: }
484: 
485: uint32_t lcm4(uint32_t a);
486: 
487: /**
488:  * @internal
489:  * @~English
490:  * @brief Callback for optimally tiled textures with possible source row
491:  *        padding.
492:  *
493:  * Copies data to the staging buffer removing row padding, if necessary.
494:  * Increments the offset for destination of the next copy increasing it to an
495:  * appropriate common multiple of the element size and 4 to comply with Vulkan
496:  * valid usage. Finally sets up a region to copy the face/lod from the staging
497:  * buffer to the final image.
498:  *
499:  * This longer method is needed because row padding is different between
500:  * KTX (pad to 4) and Vulkan (none). Also region->bufferOffset, i.e. the start
501:  * of each image, has to be a multiple of 4 and also a multiple of the
502:  * element size.
503:  *
504:  * This should be used with @c ktx_Texture_IterateFaceLevels or
505:  * @c ktx_Texture_IterateLoadLevelFaces. Face-level iteration has been
506:  * selected to minimize the buffering needed between reading the file and
507:  * copying the data into the staging buffer. Obviously when
508:  * @c ktx_Texture_IterateFaceLevels is being used, this is a moot point.
509: *
510:  * @copydetails PFNKTXITERCB
511:  */
512: KTX_error_code
513: optimalTilingPadCallback(int miplevel, int face,
514:                          int width, int height, int depth,
515:                          ktx_uint64_t faceLodSize,
516:                          void* pixels, void* userdata)
517: {
518:     user_cbdata_optimal* ud = (user_cbdata_optimal*)userdata;
519:     ktx_uint32_t rowPitch = width * ud->elementSize;
520: 
521:     // Set bufferOffset in destination region in final image
522: #if defined(_DEBUG)
523:     assert(ud->region < ud->regionsArrayEnd);
524: #endif
525:     ud->region->bufferOffset = ud->offset;
526: 
527:     // Copy data into staging buffer
528:     if (_KTX_PAD_UNPACK_ALIGN_LEN(rowPitch) == 0) {
529:         // No padding. Can copy in bulk.
530:         memcpy(ud->dest + ud->offset, pixels, faceLodSize);
531:         ud->offset += faceLodSize;
532:     } else {
533:         // Must remove padding. Copy a row at a time.
534: 		ktx_uint32_t image, imageIterations;
535: 		ktx_int32_t row;
536:         ktx_uint32_t paddedRowPitch;
537: 
538:         if (ud->numDimensions == 3)
539:             imageIterations = depth;
540:         else if (ud->numLayers > 1)
541:             imageIterations = ud->numLayers * ud->numFaces;
542:         else
543:             imageIterations = 1;
544:         rowPitch = paddedRowPitch = width * ud->elementSize;
545:         paddedRowPitch = _KTX_PAD_UNPACK_ALIGN(paddedRowPitch);
546:         for (image = 0; image < imageIterations; image++) {
547:             for (row = 0; row < height; row++) {
548:                 memcpy(ud->dest + ud->offset, pixels, rowPitch);
549:                 ud->offset += rowPitch;
550:                 pixels = (ktx_uint8_t*)pixels + paddedRowPitch;
551:             }
552:         }
553:     }
554: 
555:     // Round to needed multiples for next region, if necessary.
556:     if (ud->offset % ud->elementSize != 0 || ud->offset % 4 != 0) {
557:         // Only elementSizes of 1,2 and 3 will bring us here.
558:         assert(ud->elementSize < 4 && ud->elementSize > 0);
559:         ktx_uint32_t lcm = lcm4(ud->elementSize);
560:         ud->offset = _KTX_PADN(lcm, ud->offset);
561:     }
562:     // These 2 are expressed in texels; not suitable for dealing with padding.
563:     ud->region->bufferRowLength = 0;
564:     ud->region->bufferImageHeight = 0;
565:     ud->region->imageSubresource.aspectMask = VK_IMAGE_ASPECT_COLOR_BIT;
566:     ud->region->imageSubresource.mipLevel = miplevel;
567:     ud->region->imageSubresource.baseArrayLayer = face;
568:     ud->region->imageSubresource.layerCount = ud->numLayers * ud->numFaces;
569:     ud->region->imageOffset.x = 0;
570:     ud->region->imageOffset.y = 0;
571:     ud->region->imageOffset.z = 0;
572:     ud->region->imageExtent.width = width;
573:     ud->region->imageExtent.height = height;
574:     ud->region->imageExtent.depth = depth;
575: 
576:     ud->region += 1;
577: 
578:     return KTX_SUCCESS;
579: }

597: linearTilingCallback(int miplevel, int face,

605:     VkImageSubresource subRes = {

630: /**
631:  * @internal
632:  * @~English
633:  * @brief Callback for linear tiled textures with possible source row
634:  *        padding.
635:  *
636:  * Need to use this long method as row padding is different
637:  * between KTX (pad to 4) and Vulkan (none).
638:  *
639:  * In theory this should work for the no-padding case too but it is much
640:  * clearer and a bit faster to use the simple callback above. It also avoids
641:  * potential Vulkan implementation bugs.
642:  *
643:  * I have seen weird subResLayout results with a BC2_UNORM texture in the only
644:  * real Vulkan implementation I have available (Mesa). The reported row & image
645:  * strides appears to be for an R8G8B8A8_UNORM of the same texel size.
646:  */
647: KTX_error_code
648: linearTilingPadCallback(int miplevel, int face,
649:                       int width, int height, int depth,
650:                       ktx_uint64_t faceLodSize,
651:                       void* pixels, void* userdata)
652: {
653:     user_cbdata_linear* ud = (user_cbdata_linear*)userdata;
654:     VkDeviceSize offset;
655:     ktx_size_t   imageSize = 0;
656:     VkDeviceSize imagePitch = 0;
657:     ktx_uint32_t srcRowPitch;
658:     ktx_uint32_t rowIterations;
659:     ktx_uint32_t imageIterations;
660:     ktx_uint32_t row, image;
661:     ktx_uint8_t* pSrc;
662:     ktx_size_t   copySize;
663:     VkSubresourceLayout subResLayout;
664: #if !defined(_MSC_VER) || _MSC_VER >= 1920
665:     VkImageSubresource subRes = {
666:       .aspectMask = VK_IMAGE_ASPECT_COLOR_BIT,
667:       .mipLevel = miplevel,
668:       .arrayLayer = face
669:     };
670: #else
671:     VkImageSubresource subRes = {0};
672:     subRes.aspectMask = VK_IMAGE_ASPECT_COLOR_BIT;
673:     subRes.mipLevel = miplevel;
674:     subRes.arrayLayer = face;
675: #endif
676: 
677:     UNUSED(width);
678: 
679:     // Get sub resources layout. Includes row pitch, size,
680:     // offsets, etc.
681:     ud->vkFuncs.vkGetImageSubresourceLayout(ud->device, ud->destImage, &subRes,
682:                                 &subResLayout);
683: 
684:     srcRowPitch = ktxTexture_GetRowPitch(ud->texture, miplevel);
685: 
686:     if (subResLayout.rowPitch != srcRowPitch)
687:         rowIterations = height;
688:     else
689:         rowIterations = 1;
690: 
691:     imageIterations = 1;
692:     // Arrays, including cube map arrays, or 3D textures
693:     // Note from the Vulkan spec:
694:     //  *  arrayPitch is undefined for images that were not
695:     //     created as arrays.
696:     //  *  depthPitch is defined only for 3D images.
697:     if (ud->texture->numLayers > 1 || ud->texture->numDimensions == 3) {
698:         imageSize = ktxTexture_GetImageSize(ud->texture, miplevel);
699:         if (ud->texture->numLayers > 1) {
700:             imagePitch = subResLayout.arrayPitch;
701:             if (imagePitch != imageSize)
702:                 imageIterations
703:                         = ud->texture->numLayers * ud->texture->numFaces;
704:         } else {
705:             imagePitch = subResLayout.depthPitch;
706:             if (imagePitch != imageSize)
707:                 imageIterations = depth;
708:         }
709:         assert(imageSize <= imagePitch);
710:     }
711: 
712:     if (rowIterations > 1) {
713:         // Copy the minimum of srcRowPitch, the GL_UNPACK_ALIGNMENT padded size,
714:         // and subResLayout.rowPitch.
715:         if (subResLayout.rowPitch < srcRowPitch)
716:             copySize = subResLayout.rowPitch;
717:         else
718:             copySize = srcRowPitch;
719:     } else if (imageIterations > 1)
720:         copySize = faceLodSize / imageIterations;
721:     else
722:         copySize = faceLodSize;
723: 
724:     offset = subResLayout.offset;
725:     // Copy image data to destImage via its mapped memory.
726:     for (image = 0; image < imageIterations; image++) {
727:         pSrc = (ktx_uint8_t*)pixels + imageSize * image;
728:         for (row = 0; row < rowIterations; row++) {
729:             memcpy(ud->dest + offset, pSrc, copySize);
730:             offset += subResLayout.rowPitch;
731:             pSrc += srcRowPitch;
732:           }
733:         offset += imagePitch;
734:     }
735:     return KTX_SUCCESS;
736: }

738: /**
739:  * @memberof ktxTexture
740:  * @~English
741:  * @brief Create a Vulkan image object from a ktxTexture object.
742:  *
743:  * Creates a VkImage with @c VkFormat etc. matching the KTX data and uploads
744:  * the images.  Mipmaps will be generated if the @c ktxTexture's
745:  * @c generateMipmaps flag is set. Returns the handles of the created objects
746:  * and information about the texture in the @c ktxVulkanTexture pointed at by
747:  * @p vkTexture.
748:  *
749:  * The created VkImage will have @c VK_SHARING_MODE_EXCLUSIVE set thus the
750:  * resulting image will be usable only with queues of the same family as
751:  * the @c queue in the ktxVulkanDeviceInfo pointed to by @a vdi.
752:  *
753:  * @p usageFlags and thus acceptable usage of the created image may be
754:  * augmented as follows:
755:  * - with @c VK_IMAGE_USAGE_TRANSFER_DST_BIT if @p tiling is
756:  *   @c VK_IMAGE_TILING_OPTIMAL
757:  * - with <code>VK_IMAGE_USAGE_TRANSFER_DST_BIT | VK_IMAGE_USAGE_TRANSFER_SRC_BIT</code>
758:  *   if @c generateMipmaps is set in the @c ktxTexture.
759:  *
760:  * Most Vulkan implementations support @c VK_IMAGE_TILING_LINEAR only for a very
761:  * limited number of formats and features. Generally @c VK_IMAGE_TILING_OPTIMAL
762:  * is preferred. The latter requires a staging buffer so will use more memory
763:  * during loading.
764:  * 
765:  * If a pointer to a set of suballocator callbacks is provided, they
766:  * will be used instead of manual allocation of VkDeviceMemory. A 64 bit uint
767:  * that references the suballocated page(s) is returned on memory procurement 
768:  * and saved in the @c allocationId field of the structure pointed to by @a vkTexture.
769:  *
770:  * @note When loading a ktxTexture1, payloads with format @c GL_COMPRESSED_RGBA_ASTC_\*_KHR
771:  * are mapped to the equivalent @c VK_FORMAT_ASTC_\*_SFLOAT_BLOCK. The calling application
772:  * must therefore enable the @c VK_EXT_texture_compression_astc_hdr extension and its
773:  * @c textureCompressionASTC_HDR feature in order to render such textures. Using these formats,
774:  * Vulkan implementations will render both HDR and LDR blocks within the texture. With
775:  * the alternative mapping to @c VK_FORMAT_ASTC_\*_UNORM_BLOCK they will render HDR
776:  * blocks in the error color.
777:  *
778:  * @param[in] This                        pointer to the ktxTexture from which to upload.
779:  * @param [in] vdi                        pointer to a ktxVulkanDeviceInfo structure providing
780:  *                                        information about the Vulkan device onto which to
781:  *                                        load the texture.
782:  * @param [in,out] vkTexture              pointer to a ktxVulkanTexture structure into which
783:  *                                        the function writes information about the created
784:  *                                        VkImage.
785:  * @param [in] tiling                     type of tiling to use in the destination image
786:  *                                        on the Vulkan device.
787:  * @param [in] usageFlags                 a set of VkImageUsageFlags bits indicating the
788:  *                                        intended usage of the destination image.
789:  * @param [in] finalLayout                a VkImageLayout value indicating the desired
790:  *                                        final layout of the created image.
791:  * @param [in] subAllocatorCallbacks      pointer to a set of suballocator callbacks 
792:  *                                        that wrap around suballocator calls: alloc, 
793:  *                                        bindbuffer, bindimage, map, unmap and free.
794:  *                                        They use a uint64_t stored in the @c allocationId
795:  *                                        field of the structure pointed at by @a vkTexture
796:  *                                        to reference allocated page(s).
797:  *
798:  * @return  KTX_SUCCESS on success, other KTX_* enum values on error.
799:  *
800:  * @exception KTX_INVALID_VALUE         An incomplete set of callbacks are provided in 
801:  *                                      subAllocatorCallbacks.
802:  * @exception KTX_INVALID_VALUE         @p This, @p vdi or @p vkTexture is @c NULL.
803:  * @exception KTX_INVALID_OPERATION     The ktxTexture contains neither images nor
804:  *                                      an active stream from which to read them.
805:  * @exception KTX_INVALID_OPERATION     The combination of the ktxTexture's format,
806:  *                                      @p tiling and @p usageFlags is not supported
807:  *                                      by the physical device.
808:  * @exception KTX_INVALID_OPERATION     Requested mipmap generation is not supported
809:  *                                      by the physical device for the combination
810:  *                                      of the ktxTexture's format and @p tiling.
811:  * @exception KTX_INVALID_OPERATION     Number of mip levels or array layers exceeds
812:  *                                      the maximums supported for the ktxTexture's
813:  *                                      format and @p tiling.
814:  * @exception KTX_OUT_OF_MEMORY         Sufficient memory could not be allocated on
815:  *                                      either the CPU or the Vulkan device.
816:  * @exception KTX_UNSUPPORTED_FEATURE   Attempting to sparsely bind KTX textures
817:  *                                      for the time being will report this error.
818:  *
819:  * @sa @ref ktxVulkanDeviceInfo::ktxVulkanDeviceInfo\_Construct "ktxVulkanDeviceInfo_Construct()"
820:  */
821: KTX_error_code
822: ktxTexture_VkUploadEx_WithSuballocator(ktxTexture* This, ktxVulkanDeviceInfo* vdi,
823:                                        ktxVulkanTexture* vkTexture,
824:                                        VkImageTiling tiling,
825:                                        VkImageUsageFlags usageFlags,
826:                                        VkImageLayout finalLayout,
827:                                        ktxVulkanTexture_subAllocatorCallbacks* subAllocatorCallbacks)
828: {
829:     KTX_error_code           kResult;
830:     VkFilter                 blitFilter = VK_FILTER_LINEAR;
831:     VkFormat                 vkFormat;
832:     VkImageType              imageType;
833:     VkImageViewType          viewType;
834:     VkImageCreateFlags       createFlags = 0;
835:     VkImageFormatProperties  imageFormatProperties;
836:     VkResult                 vResult;
837:     VkCommandBufferBeginInfo cmdBufBeginInfo = {
838:         .sType = VK_STRUCTURE_TYPE_COMMAND_BUFFER_BEGIN_INFO,
839:         .pNext = NULL
840:     };
841:     VkImageCreateInfo        imageCreateInfo = {
842:          .sType = VK_STRUCTURE_TYPE_IMAGE_CREATE_INFO,
843:          .pNext = NULL
844:     };
845:     VkMemoryAllocateInfo     memAllocInfo = {
846:         .sType = VK_STRUCTURE_TYPE_MEMORY_ALLOCATE_INFO,
847:         .pNext = NULL,
848:         .allocationSize = 0,
849:         .memoryTypeIndex = 0
850:     };
851:     VkMemoryRequirements     memReqs;
852:     ktx_uint32_t             numImageLayers, numImageLevels;
853:     ktx_uint32_t elementSize = ktxTexture_GetElementSize(This);
854:     ktx_bool_t               canUseFasterPath;
855:     ktx_bool_t               useSuballocator = false;
856:     if (subAllocatorCallbacks) {
857:         if (subAllocatorCallbacks->allocMemFuncPtr &&
858:             subAllocatorCallbacks->bindBufferFuncPtr &&
859:             subAllocatorCallbacks->bindImageFuncPtr &&
860:             subAllocatorCallbacks->memoryMapFuncPtr &&
861:             subAllocatorCallbacks->memoryUnmapFuncPtr &&
862:             subAllocatorCallbacks->freeMemFuncPtr)
863:             useSuballocator = true;
864:         else
865:             return KTX_INVALID_VALUE;
866:     }
867: 
868:     if (!vdi || !This || !vkTexture) {
869:         return KTX_INVALID_VALUE;
870:     }
871: 
872:     if (!This->pData && !ktxTexture_isActiveStream(This)) {
873:         /* Nothing to upload. */
874:         return KTX_INVALID_OPERATION;
875:     }
876: 
877:     /* _ktxCheckHeader should have caught this. */
878:     assert(This->numFaces == 6 ? This->numDimensions == 2 : VK_TRUE);
879: 
880:     numImageLayers = This->numLayers;
881:     if (This->isCubemap) {
882:         numImageLayers *= 6;
883:         createFlags = VK_IMAGE_CREATE_CUBE_COMPATIBLE_BIT;
884:     }
885: 
886:     assert(This->numDimensions >= 1 && This->numDimensions <= 3);
887:     switch (This->numDimensions) {
888:       case 1:
889:         imageType = VK_IMAGE_TYPE_1D;
890:         viewType = This->isArray ?
891:                         VK_IMAGE_VIEW_TYPE_1D_ARRAY : VK_IMAGE_VIEW_TYPE_1D;
892:         break;
893:       case 2:
894:       default: // To keep compilers happy.
895:         imageType = VK_IMAGE_TYPE_2D;
896:         if (This->isCubemap)
897:             viewType = This->isArray ?
898:                         VK_IMAGE_VIEW_TYPE_CUBE_ARRAY : VK_IMAGE_VIEW_TYPE_CUBE;
899:         else
900:             viewType = This->isArray ?
901:                         VK_IMAGE_VIEW_TYPE_2D_ARRAY : VK_IMAGE_VIEW_TYPE_2D;
902:         break;
903:       case 3:
904:         imageType = VK_IMAGE_TYPE_3D;
905:         /* 3D array textures not supported in Vulkan. Attempts to create or
906:          * load them should have been trapped long before this.
907:          */
908:         assert(!This->isArray);
909:         viewType = VK_IMAGE_VIEW_TYPE_3D;
910:         break;
911:     }
912: 
913:     vkFormat = ktxTexture_GetVkFormat(This);
914:     if (vkFormat == VK_FORMAT_UNDEFINED) {
915:         return KTX_INVALID_OPERATION;
916:     }
917: 
918:     /* Get device properties for the requested image format */
919:     if (tiling == VK_IMAGE_TILING_OPTIMAL) {
920:         // Ensure we can copy from staging buffer to image.
921:         usageFlags |= VK_IMAGE_USAGE_TRANSFER_DST_BIT;
922:     }
923:     if (This->generateMipmaps) {
924:         // Ensure we can blit between levels.
925:         usageFlags |= (VK_IMAGE_USAGE_TRANSFER_DST_BIT | VK_IMAGE_USAGE_TRANSFER_SRC_BIT);
926:     }
927:     vResult = vdi->vkFuncs.vkGetPhysicalDeviceImageFormatProperties(vdi->physicalDevice,
928:                                                       vkFormat,
929:                                                       imageType,
930:                                                       tiling,
931:                                                       usageFlags,
932:                                                       createFlags,
933:                                                       &imageFormatProperties);
934:     if (vResult == VK_ERROR_FORMAT_NOT_SUPPORTED) {
935:         return KTX_INVALID_OPERATION;
936:     }
937:     if (This->numLayers > imageFormatProperties.maxArrayLayers) {
938:         return KTX_INVALID_OPERATION;
939:     }
940: 
941:     if (This->generateMipmaps) {
942:         uint32_t max_dim;
943:         VkFormatProperties    formatProperties;
944:         VkFormatFeatureFlags  formatFeatureFlags;
945:         VkFormatFeatureFlags  neededFeatures
946:             = VK_FORMAT_FEATURE_BLIT_DST_BIT | VK_FORMAT_FEATURE_BLIT_SRC_BIT;
947:         vdi->vkFuncs.vkGetPhysicalDeviceFormatProperties(vdi->physicalDevice,
948:                                             vkFormat,
949:                                             &formatProperties);
950:         assert(vResult == VK_SUCCESS);
951:         if (tiling == VK_IMAGE_TILING_OPTIMAL)
952:             formatFeatureFlags = formatProperties.optimalTilingFeatures;
953:         else
954:             formatFeatureFlags = formatProperties.linearTilingFeatures;
955: 
956:         if ((formatFeatureFlags & neededFeatures) != neededFeatures)
957:             return KTX_INVALID_OPERATION;
958: 
959:         if (formatFeatureFlags & VK_FORMAT_FEATURE_SAMPLED_IMAGE_FILTER_LINEAR_BIT)
960:             blitFilter = VK_FILTER_LINEAR;
961:         else
962:             blitFilter = VK_FILTER_NEAREST; // XXX INVALID_OP?
963: 
964:         max_dim = MAX(MAX(This->baseWidth, This->baseHeight), This->baseDepth);
965:         numImageLevels = (uint32_t)floor(log2(max_dim)) + 1;
966:     } else {
967:         numImageLevels = This->numLevels;
968:     }
969: 
970:     if (numImageLevels > imageFormatProperties.maxMipLevels) {
971:         return KTX_INVALID_OPERATION;
972:     }
973: 
974:     if (This->classId == ktxTexture2_c) {
975:         canUseFasterPath = KTX_TRUE;
976:     } else {
977:         ktx_uint32_t actualRowPitch = ktxTexture_GetRowPitch(This, 0);
978:         ktx_uint32_t tightRowPitch = elementSize * This->baseWidth;
979:         // If the texture's images do not have any row padding, we can use a
980:         // faster path. Only uncompressed textures might have padding.
981:         //
982:         // The first test in the if will match compressed textures, because
983:         // they all have a block size that is a multiple of 4, as well as
984:         // a class of uncompressed textures that will never need padding.
985:         //
986:         // The second test matches textures whose level 0 has no padding. Any
987:         // texture whose block size is not a multiple of 4 will need padding
988:         // at some miplevel even if level 0 does not. So, if more than 1 level
989:         // exists, we must use the slower path.
990:         //
991:         // Note all elementSizes > 4 Will be a multiple of 4, so only
992:         // elementSizes of 1, 2 & 3 are a concern here.
993:         if (elementSize % 4 == 0  /* There'll be no padding at any level. */
994:                /* There is no padding at level 0 and no other levels. */
995:             || (This->numLevels == 1 && actualRowPitch == tightRowPitch))
996:             canUseFasterPath = KTX_TRUE;
997:         else
998:             canUseFasterPath = KTX_FALSE;
999:     }
1000: 
1001:     vkTexture->width = This->baseWidth;
1002:     vkTexture->height = This->baseHeight;
1003:     vkTexture->depth = This->baseDepth;
1004:     vkTexture->imageLayout = finalLayout;
1005:     vkTexture->imageFormat = vkFormat;
1006:     vkTexture->levelCount = numImageLevels;
1007:     vkTexture->layerCount = numImageLayers;
1008:     vkTexture->viewType = viewType;
1009:     vkTexture->vkDestroyImage = vdi->vkFuncs.vkDestroyImage;
1010:     vkTexture->vkFreeMemory = vdi->vkFuncs.vkFreeMemory;
1011: 
1012:     VK_CHECK_RESULT(
1013:             vdi->vkFuncs.vkBeginCommandBuffer(vdi->cmdBuffer, &cmdBufBeginInfo)
1014:             );
1015: 
1016:     if (tiling == VK_IMAGE_TILING_OPTIMAL)
1017:     {
1018:         // Create a host-visible staging buffer that contains the raw image data
1019:         VkBuffer stagingBuffer;
1020:         VkDeviceMemory stagingMemory = VK_NULL_HANDLE;
1021:         VkBufferImageCopy* copyRegions;
1022:         VkDeviceSize textureSize;
1023:         VkBufferCreateInfo bufferCreateInfo = {
1024:           .sType = VK_STRUCTURE_TYPE_BUFFER_CREATE_INFO,
1025:           .pNext = NULL
1026:         };
1027:         VkImageSubresourceRange subresourceRange;
1028:         VkFence copyFence;
1029:         VkFenceCreateInfo fenceCreateInfo = {
1030:             .sType = VK_STRUCTURE_TYPE_FENCE_CREATE_INFO,
1031:             .pNext = NULL,
1032:             .flags = VK_FLAGS_NONE
1033:         };
1034:         VkSubmitInfo submitInfo = {
1035:             .sType = VK_STRUCTURE_TYPE_SUBMIT_INFO,
1036:             .pNext = NULL
1037:         };
1038:         ktx_uint8_t* pMappedStagingBuffer;
1039:         ktx_uint32_t numCopyRegions;
1040:         user_cbdata_optimal cbData;
1041: 
1042: 
1043:         textureSize = ktxTexture_GetDataSizeUncompressed(This);
1044:         bufferCreateInfo.size = textureSize;
1045:         if (canUseFasterPath) {
1046:             /*
1047:              * Because all array layers and faces are the same size they can
1048:              * be copied in a single operation so there'll be 1 copy per mip
1049:              * level.
1050:              */
1051:             numCopyRegions = This->numLevels;
1052:         } else {
1053:             /*
1054:              * Have to copy all images individually into the staging
1055:              * buffer so we can place them at correct multiples of
1056:              * elementSize and 4 and also need a copy region per image
1057:              * in case they end up with padding between them.
1058:              */
1059:             numCopyRegions = This->isArray ? This->numLevels
1060:                                   : This->numLevels * This->numFaces;
1061:             /*
1062:              * Add extra space to allow for possible padding described
1063:              * above. A bit ad-hoc but it's only a small amount of
1064:              * memory.
1065:              */
1066:             bufferCreateInfo.size += numCopyRegions * elementSize * 4;
1067:         }
1068:         copyRegions = (VkBufferImageCopy*)malloc(sizeof(VkBufferImageCopy)
1069:                                                    * numCopyRegions);
1070:         if (copyRegions == NULL) {
1071:             return KTX_OUT_OF_MEMORY;
1072:         }
1073: 
1074:         // This buffer is used as a transfer source for the buffer copy
1075:         bufferCreateInfo.usage = VK_BUFFER_USAGE_TRANSFER_SRC_BIT;
1076:         bufferCreateInfo.sharingMode = VK_SHARING_MODE_EXCLUSIVE;
1077: 
1078:         VK_CHECK_RESULT(
1079:                 vdi->vkFuncs.vkCreateBuffer(vdi->device, &bufferCreateInfo,
1080:                                        vdi->pAllocator, &stagingBuffer));
1081: 
1082:         // Get memory requirements for the staging buffer (alignment,
1083:         // memory type bits)
1084:         vdi->vkFuncs.vkGetBufferMemoryRequirements(vdi->device, stagingBuffer, &memReqs);
1085: 
1086:         memAllocInfo.allocationSize = memReqs.size;
1087:         // Get memory type index for a host visible buffer
1088:         memAllocInfo.memoryTypeIndex = ktxVulkanDeviceInfo_getMemoryType(
1089:                 vdi,
1090:                 memReqs.memoryTypeBits,
1091:                 VK_MEMORY_PROPERTY_HOST_VISIBLE_BIT
1092:               | VK_MEMORY_PROPERTY_HOST_COHERENT_BIT
1093:         );
1094: 
1095:         uint64_t stagingAllocId = 0ull;
1096:         if (!useSuballocator) {
1097:             vResult = vdi->vkFuncs.vkAllocateMemory(vdi->device, &memAllocInfo,
1098:                 vdi->pAllocator, &stagingMemory);
1099:             if (vResult != VK_SUCCESS) {
1100:                 free(copyRegions);
1101:                 return KTX_OUT_OF_MEMORY;
1102:             }
1103:             VK_CHECK_RESULT(
1104:                     vdi->vkFuncs.vkBindBufferMemory(vdi->device, stagingBuffer,
1105:                         stagingMemory, 0));
1106: 
1107:             VK_CHECK_RESULT(
1108:                     vdi->vkFuncs.vkMapMemory(vdi->device, stagingMemory, 0,
1109:                         memReqs.size, 0,
1110:                         (void**)&pMappedStagingBuffer));
1111:         }
1112:         else {
1113:             uint64_t numPages = 0ull;
1114:             stagingAllocId = subAllocatorCallbacks->allocMemFuncPtr(&memAllocInfo, &memReqs, &numPages);
1115:             if (stagingAllocId == 0ull) {
1116:                 free(copyRegions);
1117:                 return KTX_OUT_OF_MEMORY;
1118:             }
1119:             if (numPages > 1ull) { // Sparse binding of KTX textures is unsupported for the moment
1120:                 free(copyRegions);
1121:                 return KTX_UNSUPPORTED_FEATURE;
1122:             }
1123:             VK_CHECK_RESULT(
1124:                 subAllocatorCallbacks->bindBufferFuncPtr(stagingBuffer, stagingAllocId));
1125:             VK_CHECK_RESULT(
1126:                 subAllocatorCallbacks->memoryMapFuncPtr(stagingAllocId, 0ull, 
1127:                 &memReqs.size,
1128:                 (void**)&pMappedStagingBuffer));
1129:         }
1130: 
1131:         cbData.offset = 0;
1132:         cbData.region = copyRegions;
1133:         cbData.numFaces = This->numFaces;
1134:         cbData.numLayers = This->numLayers;
1135:         cbData.dest = pMappedStagingBuffer;
1136:         cbData.elementSize = elementSize;
1137:         cbData.numDimensions = This->numDimensions;
1138: #if defined(_DEBUG)
1139:         cbData.regionsArrayEnd = copyRegions + numCopyRegions;
1140: #endif
1141:         if (canUseFasterPath) {
1142:             // Bulk load the data to the staging buffer and iterate
1143:             // over levels.
1144: 
1145:             if (This->pData) {
1146:                 // Image data has already been loaded. Copy to staging
1147:                 // buffer.
1148:                 assert(This->dataSize <= memAllocInfo.allocationSize);
1149:                 memcpy(pMappedStagingBuffer, This->pData, This->dataSize);
1150:             } else {
1151:                 /* Load the image data directly into the staging buffer. */
1152:                 /* The strange cast quiets an Xcode warning when building
1153:                  * for the Generic iOS Device where size_t is 32-bit even
1154:                  * when building for arm64. */
1155:                 kResult = ktxTexture_LoadImageData(This,
1156:                                       pMappedStagingBuffer,
1157:                                       (ktx_size_t)memAllocInfo.allocationSize);
1158:                 if (kResult != KTX_SUCCESS)
1159:                     return kResult;
1160:             }
1161: 
1162:             // Iterate over mip levels to set up the copy regions.
1163:             kResult = ktxTexture_IterateLevels(This,
1164:                                                optimalTilingCallback,
1165:                                                &cbData);
